title: A friend's death (Confessions 4.4)
hook: his friend dies, and everything he looks at is death; he had become a great question to himself
tomorrow: can you shut your eyes and still get hooked?

segments.voice: Carthage sizzled like a cauldron, and Augustine was hungry for something he couldn't name. Your line: in love with love. Today, love meets loss, so go gently.

A name still saved in a phone, from someone who won't text back. Augustine had a friend he'd known since they were boys at school together. Now the friend lies unconscious with a fever, and while he's out, he's baptized. He wakes a little better. Augustine, sure his friend will laugh it off with him, makes a joke about the baptism. The friend looks at him as if he were an enemy: if you want to stay my friend, don't talk to me like that. Augustine decides to bring it up when he's well. A few days later, while Augustine is away, the fever comes back.
screen: `A NAME THAT WON'T TEXT BACK.` → `A JOKE THAT LANDS WRONG.` → `THE FEVER COMES BACK.`

segments.voice: And his friend dies. Book Four never gives the friend's name. It gives the grief. Augustine's heart went dark, he says, and whatever he looked at was death. That's the answer to yesterday's question. His hometown became a torment. His father's house, a strange misery. Everything they'd shared turned to pain without his friend. His eyes kept looking for him everywhere, and no place could say, look, he's coming, the way it used to when his friend was only away. Then the line the carry is built on: I had become a great question to myself. He asks his own soul why it's so sad, and it has no answer. Only tears were sweet to him, he says; they had taken his friend's place. Here's the thing worth telling someone. Augustine is writing years later, as a man of prayer, and he could have skipped straight to the comfort. He doesn't. He lets the question stand on the page, in a book spoken to God. The grief isn't tidied up or explained away. It's told, honestly, to someone listening.
screen: `HE IS NEVER NAMED.` · `WHATEVER I LOOKED AT WAS DEATH.` · `A GREAT QUESTION TO MYSELF.` · `NOT TIDIED UP, JUST TOLD.` · then, large: `I BECAME A QUESTION.`

segments.voice: If you're missing someone, find one thing that holds them, a photo, an old message, something they gave you, and look at it for the sit. Let the question stay a question. If that's too heavy today, choose a smaller memory, or just rest with your breath.
A friend's death. Augustine's grief in Book Four: a friend with no name on the page, and a man who became a question to himself.
Carry this: I became a question, and in Augustine's book, grief gets told, not tidied. Take care tonight.
